description: Machine-readable SQL feature matrix for the MinnowDatabase engine. Every entry carries an example; the conformance test executes supported examples through both executors and asserts that each unsupported example still fails with the recorded error fragment. Entries marked unsupported describe the SQL surface only: some carry a note explaining that the capability exists through a typed API instead, or that the restriction is deliberate.

features.example: SELECT region, amount FROM rows
SELECT amount AS total FROM rows
SELECT * FROM rows
SELECT DISTINCT region FROM rows
SELECT (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM rows) AS peak FROM rows LIMIT 1
SELECT amount * 2 + 1 AS scaled FROM rows
SELECT ROUND(amount / 3, 2) AS thirds FROM rows
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region = 'west'
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount >= 10
SELECT active, amount FROM rows WHERE active = TRUE
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region != NULL
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE joined >= DATE '2026-01-01'
SELECT region, amount FROM rows WHERE amount >= $1 ORDER BY amount
features.notes: Values bind by 1-based number and may repeat; the compiled plan is cached on the SQL text and re-bound per execution.

features.example: SELECT region, amount FROM rows WHERE amount >= ? AND active = ? ORDER BY amount
features.notes: Each ? takes the next value in order. A statement uses either ? or $n placeholders, never both; PostgreSQL itself has no ? form.

features.example: SELECT r.region, d.label FROM rows r JOIN dims d ON d.region = r.region
SELECT r.region, d.label FROM rows r LEFT JOIN dims d ON d.region = r.region
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount > 5 AND region = 'west'
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region IN ('west', 'east')
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region NOT IN ('north')
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region IN (SELECT region FROM dims)
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount > (SELECT AVG(amount) FROM rows)
SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS count FROM rows GROUP BY region
SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS total FROM rows GROUP BY ROLLUP(region)
features.notes: ROLLUP/CUBE/GROUPING SETS desugar into a UNION ALL of grouped blocks. The GROUPING() marker is deliberately unsupported, so rollup NULLs and data NULLs are indistinguishable. SQLite itself has none of these.

features.example: SELECT region, active, COUNT(*) AS c FROM rows GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((region), (active), ())
SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS count FROM rows GROUP BY region HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM rows
SELECT SUM(amount) AS total FROM rows
SELECT AVG(amount) AS mean FROM rows
SELECT MIN(amount) AS low, MAX(amount) AS high FROM rows
SELECT region, amount FROM rows ORDER BY region, amount DESC
SELECT * FROM rows ORDER BY amount
SELECT amount FROM rows ORDER BY amount LIMIT 2
WITH west AS (SELECT amount FROM rows WHERE region = 'west') SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM west
WITH a AS (SELECT amount FROM rows), b AS (SELECT amount FROM a WHERE amount > 5) SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM b
SELECT d.total FROM (SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS total FROM rows GROUP BY region) d ORDER BY d.total
SELECT region FROM rows UNION SELECT region FROM dims ORDER BY region
SELECT region FROM rows UNION ALL SELECT region FROM dims
SELECT region, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY amount) AS rn FROM rows
SELECT region, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS r FROM rows
SELECT region, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS dr FROM rows
INSERT INTO keyed (name, score) VALUES ('a', 1), ('b', 2)
features.notes: Through execute(); query() stays read-only.

features.example: UPDATE keyed SET score = score + 1 WHERE score > 0
features.notes: Requires a unique-key table; read-then-mutate, not serializable.

features.example: DELETE FROM keyed WHERE score < 0
features.notes: Requires a unique-key table.

features.example: DELETE FROM keyed WHERE name = 'x' RETURNING name, score
features.notes: RETURNING works on INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE; inserts echo written values, updates return post-update values, deletes the rows as read.

features.example: INSERT INTO keyed (name, score) VALUES ('x', 9) ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET score = EXCLUDED.score
features.notes: Whole-row upsert: DO UPDATE must set every inserted column from EXCLUDED, and the conflict target is the unique key.

features.example: INSERT INTO keyed (name, score) VALUES ('x', 9), ('z', 1) ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING
features.notes: Rows whose key already exists at the statement's snapshot are skipped.

features.example: INSERT INTO keyed (name, score, bonus) VALUES ('x', 50, 9) ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET score = EXCLUDED.score
features.notes: Assigning a subset of inserted columns merges only those into existing rows; unassigned columns keep their stored values.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount > 5 OR region = 'west'
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region LIKE 'w%'
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region IS DISTINCT FROM 'west'
features.notes: Null-safe: NULL is not distinct from NULL.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE active IS TRUE OR active IS UNKNOWN
features.notes: IS [NOT] TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN never return UNKNOWN; they desugar to null-safe comparisons.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region LIKE 'we!%st' ESCAPE '!' OR region LIKE 'we%'
features.notes: ESCAPE makes the next pattern character literal, wildcards included.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount > ALL (SELECT amount FROM dims)
features.notes: ANY/SOME/ALL with full three-valued logic; correlated forms are rejected. SQLite itself has no quantified comparisons.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region ILIKE 'WE%'
features.notes: Case-insensitive LIKE, a PostgreSQL extension; SQLite's LIKE is case-insensitive by default instead.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE MATCH(region) AGAINST 'west'
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE MATCH(*) AGAINST 'wes*'
SELECT region, BM25(region) AGAINST 'west' AS score FROM rows WHERE MATCH(region) AGAINST 'west' ORDER BY score DESC
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount > 0 ORDER BY amount * 2 DESC, region
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount BETWEEN 1 AND 5
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE amount BETWEEN SYMMETRIC 5 AND 1
features.notes: SYMMETRIC accepts the bounds in either order.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE region IS NULL
SELECT amount FROM rows WHERE region IS NOT NULL
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dims)
features.notes: Uncorrelated EXISTS only; correlated references still fail as unknown aliases.

features.example: SELECT CASE WHEN amount > 5 THEN 'big' ELSE 'small' END AS size FROM rows
SELECT region FROM rows r WHERE amount > (SELECT AVG(amount) FROM rows q WHERE q.region = r.region)
features.notes: Equality-correlated subqueries decorrelate into derived-table joins at compile time; both executors run plain joins.

features.example: SELECT amount FROM rows r WHERE EXISTS (SELECT region FROM dims d WHERE d.region = r.region)
features.notes: EXISTS joins the subquery's distinct correlation keys; NOT EXISTS becomes a left join checked with IS NULL.

features.example: SELECT r.region, (SELECT AVG(q.amount) FROM rows q WHERE q.region = r.region) AS regional FROM rows r
features.notes: Correlated scalar aggregates decorrelate in the select list too, outside grouped queries.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows r WHERE EXISTS (SELECT region FROM dims d WHERE d.amount > r.amount)
features.notes: Correlation must be a plain equality between one inner and one outer qualified column.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows r WHERE region NOT IN (SELECT d.region FROM dims d WHERE d.region = r.region)
features.notes: Correlated NOT IN has NULL semantics that the join rewrite cannot preserve; NOT EXISTS expresses the intent.

features.example: WITH RECURSIVE n AS (SELECT MIN(amount) AS v FROM rows UNION ALL SELECT v + 1 FROM n WHERE v < 6) SELECT v FROM n
features.notes: Linear delta recursion with UNION or UNION ALL, capped at 10,000 iterations and 1,000,000 rows. Plain WITH still rejects self-references.

features.example: WITH totals AS (SELECT MAX(score) AS top FROM keyed) DELETE FROM keyed WHERE score >= (SELECT top FROM totals) RETURNING name
features.notes: WITH precedes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; the CTEs are visible to the statement's queries and subqueries.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows INTERSECT SELECT region FROM dims
features.notes: INTERSECT binds tighter than UNION and EXCEPT, per the SQL standard.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows EXCEPT SELECT region FROM dims
SELECT region FROM rows INTERSECT ALL SELECT region FROM dims
features.notes: Bag semantics; SQLite itself has no INTERSECT ALL.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows EXCEPT ALL SELECT region FROM dims
features.notes: Bag semantics; SQLite itself has no EXCEPT ALL.

features.example: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT region) AS regions FROM rows
SELECT region, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE amount > 5) AS big FROM rows GROUP BY region
features.notes: Desugars into a CASE inside the aggregate, so it works with every aggregate and DISTINCT.

features.example: SELECT SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS total FROM rows
features.notes: Default frame only: whole partition without OVER ordering, running with peers when ordered.

features.example: SELECT amount, FIRST_VALUE(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY amount) AS lowest, LAST_VALUE(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY amount ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS highest FROM rows
features.notes: FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE respect the frame; the default frame ends at the current peer group, as the standard specifies.

features.example: SELECT amount, NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS half FROM rows
SELECT amount, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS pr, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS cd FROM rows
SELECT amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY amount, joined ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS windowed FROM rows
features.notes: ROWS frames take row-distance bounds; RANGE frames take UNBOUNDED and CURRENT ROW bounds, where CURRENT ROW spans the ordering peer group.

features.example: SELECT r.region FROM rows r RIGHT JOIN dims d ON d.region = r.region
features.notes: Desugars to the mirrored LEFT JOIN; supported as the sole join of a block.

features.example: SELECT r.region FROM rows r JOIN dims d ON d.amount > r.amount
features.notes: Executes as a nested-loop join (probe x build); equalities keep the hash path.

features.example: SELECT DISTINCT * FROM rows
features.notes: Expands to DISTINCT over every wildcard output column once input schemas are known.

features.example: SELECT amount FROM rows LIMIT 5 OFFSET 2
features.notes: OFFSET is accepted directly after LIMIT.

features.example: SELECT 1 + 1 AS two, UPPER('minnow') AS name
SELECT v.column1 AS n, v.column2 AS tag FROM (VALUES (1, 'one'), (2, 'two')) v
features.notes: VALUES works standalone, as a set-operation member, and as a derived table with AS alias(col, ...) renaming; columns default to column1..columnN.

features.example: SELECT region, amount FROM rows ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, amount LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2
features.notes: LIMIT and OFFSET take placeholders; the plan re-binds per execution like any parameter.

features.example: SELECT amount FROM rows ORDER BY amount OFFSET 1 ROWS FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS ONLY
features.notes: The standard fetch clause is a spelling of LIMIT; SQLite itself only speaks LIMIT.

features.example: SELECT amount FROM rows ORDER BY amount OFFSET 2
features.notes: OFFSET no longer requires LIMIT. SQLite itself needs LIMIT -1 OFFSET n.

features.example: CREATE TABLE made (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT NOT NULL, at TIMESTAMP)
features.notes: Standard type names map onto the four logical types (widths parse and are ignored); one PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE column becomes the unique key. Dropping or altering tables stays a programmatic concern.

features.example: UPDATE rows SET amount = 1
features.error: UPDATE requires a table with a unique key
features.notes: Deliberate: mutation segments address rows by unique key, so tables without one cannot be updated or deleted through any API.

features.example: CREATE TRIGGER keyed_audit AFTER INSERT ON keyed BEGIN INSERT INTO rows (region, amount) VALUES (NEW.name, NEW.score); END
features.notes: AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE row triggers with INSERT ... VALUES bodies over NEW/OLD references, executed atomically inside the triggering commit. Bodies target keyless tables; cascades and BEFORE triggers are rejected.

features.example: DROP TRIGGER droppable_audit
setup: CREATE TRIGGER droppable_audit AFTER INSERT ON keyed BEGIN INSERT INTO rows (region, amount) VALUES (NEW.name, NEW.score); END

features.example: BEGIN
features.notes: Transactions are a programmatic API.

features.example: SELECT region FROM rows WHERE (amount > 5 AND region = 'west')
SELECT region FROM rows WHERE NOT active = TRUE
SELECT region || '-' || label AS tag FROM dims
features.notes: || concatenates strings and propagates NULL; non-string operands are a type error.

features.example: SELECT amount % 3 AS remainder FROM rows
features.notes: Division and remainder by zero are NULL, matching SQLite.

features.example: SELECT CAST(amount AS INTEGER) AS whole, CAST(amount AS TEXT) AS label FROM rows
features.notes: Standard type names map to the four logical types; integer targets truncate toward zero, and non-numeric strings fail rather than becoming 0.

features.example: SELECT "region", "rows"."amount" FROM "rows" WHERE "amount" > 5
features.notes: Double-quoted identifiers are never keywords and keep their exact spelling.

features.example: SELECT region, amount FROM rows ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, amount
features.notes: Without NULLS FIRST/LAST the default matches SQLite: NULLs first ascending, last descending.

features.example: SELECT COALESCE(region, 'unknown') AS region_label FROM rows
features.notes: Arguments evaluate left to right; the first non-NULL value wins. All non-NULL arguments must share one type.

features.example: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', joined) AS joined_month FROM rows
features.notes: Units: year, quarter, month, week (Monday start), day, hour, minute, second. Truncation is in UTC; the engine has no session time zone.

features.example: SELECT UPPER(label) AS u, LOWER(label) AS l, LENGTH(label) AS n, SUBSTR(label, 2, 3) AS mid, TRIM(label) AS t FROM dims
features.notes: SUBSTRING is accepted as a spelling of SUBSTR; LENGTH and SUBSTR count characters, not UTF-16 units.

features.example: SELECT ABS(amount - 5) AS distance FROM rows
SELECT NULLIF(amount, 3) AS n, GREATEST(amount, 5) AS g, LEAST(amount, 5) AS l, FLOOR(amount) AS f, CEILING(amount) AS c, MOD(amount, 4) AS m, POWER(2, 3) AS p, SQRT(16) AS s FROM rows
features.notes: GREATEST/LEAST ignore NULL arguments, matching PostgreSQL.

features.example: SELECT REPLACE(region, 'we', 'be') AS r, LTRIM(' x') AS lt, RTRIM('x ') AS rt, INSTR(region, 'st') AS i FROM rows WHERE region IS NOT NULL
SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM joined) AS y, EXTRACT(dow FROM joined) AS d FROM rows WHERE joined IS NOT NULL
features.notes: Fields: year, quarter, month, week (ISO), day, hour, minute, second, epoch, dow — all in UTC. SQLite spells this strftime.

features.example: SELECT SUM(DISTINCT amount) AS total, region FROM rows GROUP BY region
features.notes: COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX accept DISTINCT; one DISTINCT aggregate per select, not yet combined with other aggregates or HAVING.

features.example: SELECT r.region FROM rows r JOIN dims d ON d.region = r.region AND d.amount = r.amount
features.notes: Multi-key conditions execute as a nested-loop join; single equalities keep the hash path.

features.example: SELECT r.region AS region, d.label AS label FROM rows r CROSS JOIN dims d
SELECT r.amount AS amount, d.label AS label FROM rows r FULL JOIN dims d ON d.region = r.region
features.notes: Desugars into a union of two left joins, so it must be the sole join, with an equality ON and no grouping or DISTINCT yet.

features.example: SELECT region, amount FROM rows ORDER BY 2 DESC
features.notes: Ordinals resolve to the select list at compile time; out-of-range ordinals are an error.

features.example: SELECT amount, LAG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS previous, LEAD(amount, 1, -1) OVER (ORDER BY amount) AS next FROM rows
features.notes: LAG/LEAD take a constant offset (default 1) and default value (default NULL), and require ORDER BY inside OVER.

features.example: INSERT INTO keyed (name, score) SELECT name || '2' AS name, score + 1 AS score FROM keyed
features.notes: The SELECT runs at one snapshot and materializes before the batch write.
